parsed.why: Cross-dressing offence struck down in 2022, but enforced sodomy/morality prosecutions, documented post-ruling official discrimination, continuing dress-code policing, censorship, no civil society and HIV deportation of foreigners keep exposure high.

Documented police, security-force and army violence and torture of LGBT people, militia extreme violence with near-total impunity in the east, censorship carrying imprisonment, Article 176 applied — state-tolerated targeting with no protections.

Latent, unenforced sodomy and public 'deception' offences and zero formal protections, offset by an institutionalised third-gender tradition, community shelter infrastructure and no documented police targeting.

Cross-dressing law struck down, decriminalisation politically backed, 72% acceptance and equality-group police work; but police extortion, a magistrate's courtroom exclusion, no hate-crime law and 69 recorded violence cases weigh.

Sodomy decriminalised in 2022 and a high court found SOGI discrimination unconstitutional, with Pride events, a pro-LGBT PM and inclusive visa rules; dated official hostility and one lightly-punished attack temper it.
